raw.query: WITH current_predictors AS (SELECT DISTINCT forecast_model AS model FROM provenance.v_dim WHERE is_current = TRUE AND experiment = 'predictors' AND forecast_model IS NOT NULL), coverage AS (SELECT f.resolution, f.model, f.mode, f.variate, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG((f.y_true <= f.p90)::int::double precision) AS p90_coverage FROM provenance.v_forecast_thesis_corpus f JOIN current_predictors d ON d.model = f.model WHERE f.resolution IN ('15s', '1min') AND f.p90 IS NOT NULL AND f.y_true IS NOT NULL GROUP BY f.resolution, f.model, f.mode, f.variate) SELECT resolution, COUNT(*) AS model_signal_mode_cells, MIN(p90_coverage) AS min_p90_coverage, MAX(p90_coverage) AS max_p90_coverage, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p90_coverage < 0.88 OR p90_coverage > 0.90) AS cells_outside_claimed_range, jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('model', model, 'mode', mode, 'signal', variate, 'coverage', p90_coverage) ORDER BY p90_coverage) FILTER (WHERE p90_coverage < 0.88 OR p90_coverage > 0.90) AS outside_cells FROM coverage GROUP BY resolution ORDER BY resolution
raw.claimed: p90 coverage 0.88--0.90 for every model and signal at 15-second and 1-minute resolutions
raw.evidence: The lower bounds are near nominal, but many model-signal-mode cells exceed 0.90, reaching 0.9790559549859331 at 15s and 0.9820814923907707 at 1min, so the universal calibration claim does not hold.
raw.fix: Remove 'for every model and signal' and report coverage by model family, signal, mode, and resolution, explicitly identifying the substantially over-covering baselines.
